## Theoretical and empirical estimands {#what-is-your-estimand}

```{r}
#| label: lundberg-pipeline
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3
# Lundberg et al. (2021) three steps as boxes-and-arrows (ggplot, editable).
steps <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3),
  lab = c("Theoretical\nestimand",
          "Empirical\nestimand",
          "Estimation\nstrategy"),
  sub = c("unit quantity +\ntarget population",
          "identification\nassumptions (DAG)",
          "where the R\ncode enters")
)
ggplot2::ggplot(steps, ggplot2::aes(x, 1)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(width = 0.8, height = 0.7, fill = ncl_blue) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = lab), colour = "white", fontface = "bold",
            size = 5.2, vjust = -0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sub), colour = "white", size = 3.6, vjust = 2.0) +
  ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = 1.42, xend = 1.58, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = 2.42, xend = 2.58, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 3.5)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_void()
```

::: {.none}
- The theoretical estimand is stated **outside** any model – before R opens
:::

::: {.src}
@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand.
:::

::: notes
Our five analysts and the twenty-nine red-card teams were all handed a question in words, and none of them was told exactly which quantity would answer it. Lundberg and colleagues call that quantity the estimand, and the title of their paper asks for it directly, "What is your estimand?" They divide the answer into three steps. The theoretical estimand is a unit-specific quantity and a target population, stated in plain words before any model exists. The empirical estimand is what corresponds to that quantity in the observable data, and making that link brings the assumptions of identification into the open, which is the job of the causal graph. Only the third step, estimation, opens R. When the three authors reviewed the thirty-two quantitative articles in the 2018 volume of the American Sociological Review, they could state the unit-specific quantity with confidence in only five.
:::
